findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Every legacy_email value still stored in production rows (the column was filled by the 2023 import, only no longer written) is destroyed when the migration runs, and nothing can bring it back: unlike migrations/0004_accounts.down.sql, there is no 0005 down migration, and neither the proposal nor tasks.md has a backup step. Add migrations/0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql (`ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN legacy_email TEXT;`), and before the drop copy the data out (e.g. `CREATE TABLE users_legacy_email_backup AS SELECT id, legacy_email FROM users WHERE legacy_email IS NOT NULL;`) or state in the plan why the data may be lost and how to recover it.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup

findings.recommendation: Every existing consumer of the public HTTP API that reads `account.user_name` gets a missing field after deployment, with no warning: the proposal's release note lists it only as "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase." with no **BREAKING** item and no instruction for consumers, and the change ships rename and removal in one step, so old clients cannot keep working side by side. Mark it **BREAKING** in the release note with what consumers must do, and either keep emitting the old field for a deprecation window (serialize both `user_name` and `userName`, e.g. a second deprecated field or a custom Serialize) or version the endpoint; `#[serde(alias)]` does not help here since it only affects deserialization.
findings.title: JSON field user_name renamed userName with no BREAKING mark or transition
